Ministry of Textiles Organized Workshops on Cyber Security & Secure Digital Disposal and E-Waste Management Awareness under Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
As part of Special Campaign 6, the Ministry of Textiles organised workshops on E-Waste Management Awareness and Cyber Security & Secure Digital Disposal on 15 October 2026, with the participation of over 85 officials, including all Nodal Officers. The workshops aimed to promote responsible e-waste management, strengthen cyber security awareness and encourage safe digital practices in the workplace.
A dedicated Cyber Security Awareness Session was organised to familiarise officials and staff with emerging cyber threats, including phishing attacks, malware, fraudulent WhatsApp messages and digital arrest scams. The session highlighted the importance of identifying suspicious emails, links, attachments and messages, particularly those impersonating known contacts or seeking money, one-time passwords (OTPs) or personal information.
Participants were advised to exercise caution while handling digital communications, refrain from clicking on unknown links or downloading unverified files, avoid sharing sensitive information, and verify the authenticity of suspicious communications before taking any action. The session also emphasised the importance of cyber hygiene, vigilance and the timely reporting of cyber incidents to safeguard official and personal information.
The E-Waste Management Awareness session sensitised officials to the adverse environmental impact of improper e-waste disposal, including soil and water contamination and the release of hazardous substances that may pose risks to human health and ecosystems. They highlighted the importance of resource conservation through the reuse, refurbishment and recycling of electronic equipment, wherever feasible, to recover valuable materials, reduce the demand for raw materials and minimise the volume of waste sent to landfills. Officials were also made aware of the need for proper segregation, safe handling and disposal of obsolete electronic and electrical equipment through authorised channels, in accordance with applicable e-waste management rules.
The sessions encouraged the adoption of sustainable office practices, emphasising that responsible e-waste management contributes to environmental protection, efficient resource utilisation and the promotion of a circular economy.
These initiatives reflect the Ministry of Textiles’ commitment to promoting a cleaner workplace, ensuring responsible resource management and fostering a secure digital environment. By integrating environmental sustainability with cyber security awareness, the Ministry continues to advance the objectives of Special Campaign 6 through improved workplace practices, resource conservation and enhanced digital safety.
The Ministry has also undertaken initiatives for the collection and proper management of e-waste generated within its premises, emphasising the responsible disposal of obsolete and discarded electronic and electrical equipment in accordance with applicable guidelines.

BIS Nagpur Celebrates World Standards Day 2026 with Focus on SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy
articles.full_content:
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Nagpur Branch Office, under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India, celebrated World Standards Day 2026 at Nagpur, on 14 October 2026. The celebration focused on Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7): Affordable and Clean Energy, in line with this year’s theme, “Shared Vision for a Better World.”
Observed annually on 14 October, World Standards Day recognises the collaborative efforts of experts worldwide in developing voluntary consensus-based standards that facilitate technological advancement, promote quality and safety, and support sustainable development.
The programme commenced with a welcome address by Smt. Nisha Kanbargi, Joint Director, BIS Nagpur. Shri Raunak Sukhadeve, Joint Director, BIS Nagpur, subsequently presented messages from the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), along with an overview of the significance of this year’s theme.
Dr. Manoj Kumar Rajak, Director and Head, BIS Nagpur Branch Office, outlined the objectives of the programme and highlighted the pivotal role of standardisation in bridging the gap between research and development (R&D) and industrial practices. He emphasised the need to strengthen quality infrastructure, address existing quality-related gaps, and develop Indian Standards that reflect the country’s climatic conditions, industrial requirements and practical applications.
Shri Ramchandra Ranganath Ukirde, Principal Director, National Power Training Institute (NPTI), the Chief Guest, provided insights into the prevailing energy scenario in India and globally. He discussed key challenges in the energy sector and outlined possible approaches to addressing them. He also underscored the importance of developing a skilled workforce, including trained technicians, engineers and IT professionals, to support the expansion of renewable energy. Highlighting NPTI’s initiatives, he spoke about its role in skill development, specialised training and placement opportunities for engineers in the power sector.
The inaugural session was followed by technical sessions featuring experts from leading academic and research institutions. Prof. Rajeev Agrawal, Professor of Practice in Production and Operations Management, Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Nagpur, discussed the role of effective project planning and management in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, with particular emphasis on SDG 7 and the promotion of affordable and clean energy.
Shri Abhay Kumar Kuthe, Professor (HAG), Department of Mechanical Engineering, Visvesvaraya National Institute of Technology (VNIT), Nagpur, delivered a session on product innovation in the context of SDG 7 and its societal impact. Shri. Sivaguru Prabhakaran. IAS, District Collector, Ramanathapuram inaugurated new Aadhaar Seva Kendra
articles.full_content:
Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) operationalized a new state-of-the art Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) at Ramanathapuram, on Friday, 16th October 2026 marking another step towards strengthening resident-centric Aadhaar services in the district of Ramanathapuram.
The ASK Ramanathapuram was inaugurated by Thiru. M. Sivaguru Prabhakaran. IAS, District Collector of Ramanathapuram.
He appreciated the UIDAI’s effort and interacted with residents who visited ASK as well as the centre staff present there. Also, enquired about the Aadhaar enrolment and update procedures, and reviewed the various Aadhaar services being provided at the centre.
The ASK Ramanathapuram is equipped with 4 operational kits to provide seamless Aadhaar-related services to thousands of residents. The ASK is functional on all days except public holidays, thereby ensuring greater accessibility & convenience. The Aadhaar Seva Kendra offers Aadhaar enrolment, demographic and biometric updates, grievance redressal and other Aadhaar related services under one roof.
In addition to the enrolment and update transactions, ASK Ramanathapuram will also receive grievances from Aadhaar number holders for their resolution through the Regional Office.
With the inauguration of the Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) at Ramanathapuram, UIDAI has now operationalised 24 Aadhaar Seva Kendras across Tamil Nadu. A further 06 ASKs are scheduled to become operational in the coming days across various districts, increasing the total 30 UIDAI-run Aadhaar Seva Kendras in the State.
The ASKs run by UIDAI, are designed to be fully inclusive and resident-friendly with facilities such as wheelchair accessibility, accessible restrooms, and a dedicated grievance redressal mechanism. Residents can also book appointments online for Aadhaar services at ASKs through UIDAI’s appointment portal: https://bookappointment.uidai.gov.in/ .

Also, enquired about the Aadhaar enrolment and update procedures, and reviewed the various Aadhaar services being provided at the centre.

Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 celebrated today
articles.full_content:
Event highlights the pivotal role of women farmers in advancing agricultural development and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat Union Agriculture Secretary Shri Atish Chandra highlights invaluable contributions of women to agriculture and allied sectors; emphasises the Government’s commitment to empowering women in agriculture
The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, celebrated Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 today (15 October 2026 ) at the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi, under the chairmanship of Shri Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. The programme was organised to recognise the invaluable contribution of women farmers to Indian agriculture and highlight their pivotal role in advancing agricultural development and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat.
Sh. Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in his address, highlighted the invaluable contributions of women to agriculture and allied sectors, particularly in ensuring food security, sustaining rural livelihoods, managing natural resources and driving agricultural development. He emphasised the Government’s commitment to empowering women in agriculture through various initiatives, including direct income support, affordable institutional credit, technology transfer, skill development, farm mechanisation and improved access to agricultural marketing infrastructure.

Ministry of Coal Accelerates Cleanliness And E- Waste Management efforts Under Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Coal is intensifying efforts to advance cleanliness, efficient space utilisation and responsible waste management across its offices and public sector undertakings under the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6
As part of the campaign, an e-waste collection drive was organised at a dedicated kiosk in the Main Entrance Lobby of GPOA-3, New Delhi. Union Minister of Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy and Minister of State for Coal and Mines Shri Satish Chandra Dubey participated in the drive by depositing discarded electronic items at the kiosk. The activity highlighted the importance of responsible e-waste disposal, systematic collection and scientific recycling in promoting environmental sustainability and resource efficiency.
To review the progress of the campaign, the Ministry of Coal convened a meeting with Nodal Officers from Coal India Limited (CIL) and its subsidiaries, NLC India Limited (NLCIL), Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) and the Coal Mines Provident Fund Organisation (CMPFO). The meeting assessed the status of ongoing activities and emphasised the need to expedite implementation, maintain momentum and complete all identified tasks within the stipulated timelines. Shri Sanjeev Kumar Kassi, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Coal called upon the participating organisations to intensify their efforts and ensure the timely achievement of campaign targets.
Under Special Campaign 6, CPSEs under the Ministry of Coal have made notable progress in cleanliness and space management, with 562 sites cleaned and transformed by the midpoint of the implementation phase. These efforts reflect a sustained commitment to improving workplace environments, eliminating unused and cluttered spaces, and promoting better utilisation of infrastructure across offices and field establishments.
ECL undertook a comprehensive cleaning and beautification drive across 15,000 sq. ft. in Pandaveswar Area. The activity involved the removal of wild vegetation, bushes, weeds and accumulated debris, significantly improving the cleanliness, safety and appearance of the premises.
WCL: The Security Department at WCL Headquarters transformed an underutilised space into a modern, well-organised Corporate Security Office under Special Campaign 6. The initiative demonstrates the effective utilisation of existing infrastructure to create a more functional and organised workplace.
Through these concerted efforts, the Ministry of Coal and its CPSEs are advancing the objectives of Special Campaign 6.0 by combining cleanliness drives, scientific waste management and the productive use of available spaces. The campaign continues to reinforce a culture of cleanliness, accountability and operational efficiency across the coal sector.

Press Note on Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Monthly Bulletin September 2026
articles.full_content:
Urban labour force and workforce participation strengthened Urban Female labour force participation reached highest level since October 2025 Overall UR remained stable, with a year-on-year decline
• Overall LFPR (15+ years) stood at 55.5% in September 2026, registering an increase of 0.2 percentage points over September 2025.
• Urban LFPR (15+ years) increased to 50.7% in September 2026, up from 50.4% in August 2026.
• Overall Female LFPR (15+ years) rose by 0.5 percentage points year-on-year to 34.6% in September 2026. Rural Female LFPR increased by 1.0 percentage point to 38.9% over the same period.
• Overall WPR (15+ years) increased by 0.3 percentage points year-on-year to 52.7% in September 2026.
• Overall UR (15+ years) remained stable at 5.0% in September 2026, down by 0.2 percentage points from September 2025.
• Rural Female UR declined by 0.4 percentage points year-on-year to 3.9% in September 2026, the lowest level recorded during 2026.
The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on labour force participation and employment and unemployment conditions. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for the country.
Monthly results of PLFS are released in the form of Monthly Bulletins. It presents estimates of key labour market indicators viz. Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) at the all-India level following the Current Weekly Status [1] (CWS) approach.
The Monthly Bulletins for April, 2025 to August, 2026 have already been released. The present Monthly Bulletin for September, 2026 is the eighteenth in the series.
Key findings for persons of age 15 years and above following CWS:
• Rise in urban Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):
The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for persons aged 15 years and above remained broadly stable at 55.5% in September, 2026, compared to 55.6% in August, 2026. In rural areas, LFPR was recorded at 58.0% against 58.2% in August, 2026, while the urban LFPR registered a moderate increase of 0.3 percentage points, rising from 50.4% in August, 2026 to 50.7% in September, 2026.
Over the year, the overall LFPR increased by 0.2 percentage points, from 55.3% in September, 2025 to 55.5% in September, 2026. During the same period, rural LFPR increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 57.4% to 58.0%, while urban LFPR registered a marginal decline of 0.2 percentage points, from 50.9% to 50.7%.
Urban LFPR showed a month-on-month improvement of 0.3 percentage points, reaching 50.7% in September, 2026.
• Female Labour Force Participation gains momentum in urban areas:
The overall female LFPR stood at 34.6% in September, 2026, compared with 34.8% in August, 2026. Urban female LFPR recorded a notable month-on-month increase of 0.5 percentage points, rising from 25.4% to 25.9% and reaching its highest level since

articles.title: NITI Aayog’s Frontier Tech Hub Unveils Data Centre Evaluation Framework to Help States Plan for Sustainable Growth
articles.full_content:
Framework aims to help States move from attracting data-centre investments to building investment-ready infrastructure, protecting critical resources and maximising long-term economic value
NITI Aayog’s Frontier Tech Hub has released the Data Centre Evaluation Framework on 14 October 2026 to help States plan for sustainable growth of data centres. The release took place in the presence of Prof. Abhay Karandikar, Member, NITI Aayog; Shri Anurag Jain, CEO, NITI Aayog; Ms Debjani Ghosh, Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog; representatives from the Ministry of Power, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) , Ministry of Commerce; as well as representatives from industry and the media.
The Framework, developed with inputs from industry, MeitY, Ministry of Power and DPIIT, provides State governments with a practical approach to planning, evaluating and facilitating data-centre investments. It helps them assess infrastructure readiness, safeguard critical resources and maximise long-term economic and strategic value.
India’s data-centre capacity has grown from about 375 MW in 2020 to approximately 1.5 GW currently, driven by the growing demand for Artificial Intelligence (AI), cloud computing, high-performance computing and data-intensive digital applications.
As India accelerates its AI and digital transformation, data centres are emerging as critical infrastructure underpinning the country's technological and economic ambitions. While this presents a significant opportunity, data centres at increasing scale also place substantial demands on electricity, water, land, connectivity and local infrastructure. The focus therefore needs to move beyond attracting investment to ensuring that projects are developed in locations where the necessary infrastructure and resources can support them over the long term.
The Government of India has taken important steps to create an enabling environment for data-centre investments, including a tax holiday until 2047 for eligible foreign cloud service providers leveraging India-based data-centre infrastructure. As investments grow in scale, effective State-level planning and investment readiness will be critical to ensuring sustainable growth of the sector.
Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Abhay Karandikar, Member, NITI Aayog, highlighted the opportunity to leverage data-centre investments to build India’s technological capabilities. He emphasised the need to strengthen domestic R&D, industry–academia collaboration and Indian participation across the data-centre technology value chain. He also underscored the potential for India to develop innovative solutions in advanced cooling, energy efficiency and resource-efficient computing, converting infrastructure investments into long-term economic and technological value.

The Samvad was chaired by Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS. Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), and Senior Officers from DDWS were also present during the Samvad.
In his opening remarks, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS , said that this platform has emerged as an important platform for peer learning, enabling district administrations to share innovative practices and address implementation challenges in rural drinking water service delivery. He emphasised the pivotal role of District Collectors in strengthening local water governance, ensuring effective operation and maintenance of rural water supply systems, and promoting community ownership of assets created under the Mission.
Secretary, DDWS calls for Greater Accountability and Data-Driven Governance. He directed districts to ensure regular monthly meetings of District Water and Sanitation Missions (DWSMs) and timely uploading of meeting minutes on the DWSM Portal. He also emphasised the effective utilisation of the Decision Support System (DSS) , which integrates groundwater, rainfall, hydrological and Jal Jeevan Mission data. He encouraged district administrations to use the platform for evidence-based planning, identification of water-stressed areas, source sustainability planning and prioritisation of interventions.

articles.full_content:
Kolkata, October 15, 2026
Celebrating the invaluable contributions of rural women to agriculture, fisheries and wetland-based livelihoods, ICAR-Central Inland Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR-CIFRI), Barrackpore, observed Mahila Kisan Diwas at Bartir Beel, North 24 Parganas, West Bengal, today, coinciding with the International Day of Rural Women. The programme highlighted women’s empowerment, gender equality and the potential of sustainable fisheries and responsible eco-aqua tourism to create new livelihood opportunities. Known locally as the “Dal Lake of Bengal’’, Bartir Beel is a seasonal floodplain wetland rich in aquatic biodiversity. Supporting indigenous fish, snails, crabs and diverse birdlife, the wetland also sustains seasonal agriculture as floodwaters recede. Its ecological richness and livelihood potential make it a promising landscape for integrating sustainable fisheries, wetland conservation and community-based tourism. The programme brought together 30 women farmers and rural resource users, recognising their significant contributions to agriculture, fisheries and local economic activities. Women play an important role in Rabi-season onion cultivation, undertaking nursery management, weeding, harvesting, sorting and marketing-related activities. They also contribute to jute processing, including fibre stripping, washing, sorting and drying, while participating in wetland-based livelihoods and local trade. Despite their substantial contributions, social barriers and taboos often limit women’s participation in emerging opportunities, particularly eco-aqua tourism. The interactions underscored the need for targeted capacity building, access to scientific knowledge and improved technologies, institutional support, and greater representation of women in community-level planning and decision-making. Dr. B. K. Behere, Chief Executive Officer, National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), graced the occasion as Chief Guest and emphasised the critical role of rural women in fisheries, aquaculture and livelihood development. Highlighting the principle that “Empowering women is empowering entire humanity,” he stressed that women’s empowerment is central to enhancing fish production, household nutritional security and rural well-being. Dr. Pradip Dey, Director, ICAR-CIFRI, envisioned transforming Bartir Beel into a model of women-led, science-based and ecologically sustainable rural development, recognising rural women as key stakeholders, knowledge holders and entrepreneurs.He emphasised integrating scientific fisheries management, biodiversity conservation, value addition and eco-aqua tourism to diversify livelihoods, strengthen nutritional security and generate dignified employment for women and rural youth. articles.full_content:
Bangkok, Thailand, 15 th Oct. 2026
Union Minister of Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman participated as the Governor of the World Bank in the 114 th Meeting of the Development Committee Plenary in Bangkok, Thailand, today. The agenda for the meeting was “Private Capital Mobilisation and Jobs”.
The Union Finance Minister delivered the following speech as India’s intervention on the topic of “Private Capital Mobilisation and Jobs”:
“We welcome the continued focus on mobilising private capital and creating jobs. At a time of growing energy market stress, trade fragmentation, climate pressures, and rapid technological change, productive and better-paid jobs remain the most effective pathway to poverty reduction and shared prosperity.
I wish to make six brief points.
First, jobs require ecosystems, not isolated interventions. Sustainable job creation requires high-quality and inclusive economic growth, which in turn needs macroeconomic stability, efficient infrastructure, simple and certain regulations, and broad-based access to finance and skills. Our experience shows that last-mile connectivity to energy and job markets, large-scale physical and digital public infrastructure, financial inclusion, and regulatory trust in market forces are critical for improved productivity and jobs at scale.
Second, the private sector must remain at the centre of the development agenda. Most jobs will be and should be created by private enterprises MSMEs and startups will play a big role. Mobilising private investment is therefore essential. At the same time, success should be measured not by the volume of financing mobilised, but by outcomes: jobs created and rise in productivity.
We encourage stronger collaboration among IBRD, IFC, and MIGA, and faster operationalisation of the WBG Guarantee Platform. Developing economies are constrained by a shortage of risk capital. Guarantees and risk mitigation instruments are among the most effective tools to accelerate risk-capital formation and crowding in private capital.
Third, competitive financing must remain a core priority. The World Bank must remain a development partner through competitive pricing, tapping tools like local currency financing, stronger guarantee products, and lower transaction costs. Affordable, predictable, and accessible financing must remain and at the core of the Middle-Income strategy.
Fourth, the Knowledge Bank must help address market failures. The most effective interventions from the World Bank Group would be in addressing market failures in critical areas like urbanisation, tourism, agricultural exports and critical minerals. Developing countries stand to benefit greatly from the boost to state capacity that can come from AI: it deserves much greater attention in the Bank's operational and knowledge agenda.
Fifth, we reiterate our longstanding concerns regarding Worldwide Governance Indicators and similar composite assessments. Given their far-reaching implications, there is
articles.summary: 2026 Union Minister of Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman participated as the Governor of the World Bank in the 114 th Meeting of the Development Committee Plenary in Bangkok, Thailand, today. The agenda for the meeting was “Private Capital Mobilisation and Jobs”.

articles.title: National Workshop held on “Strengthening Digital Data Systems and Evidence-Based Learning” under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihood Mission at Gurugram, Haryana on 12th and 13th October, 2026
articles.full_content:
“What gets measured gets done; what gets measured gets improved”: Secretary, Rural Development calls for robust, member-level data to drive the next phase of DAY-NRLM LokOS to evolve from a reporting platform into trusted community-finance infrastructure, backed by a stronger monitoring, evaluation and learning framework
The Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, held a two-day National Workshop on “Strengthening Digital Data Systems and Evidence-Based Learning” under DAY-NRLM, on 12th and 13th October 2026, at Gurugram, Haryana. Representatives of State Rural Livelihoods Missions, NITI Aayog, the World Bank, GIZ, J-PAL, Gates Foundation, 3ie, BRAC, NABARD, NPCI, financial institutions and development partners participated in the workshop.
In his keynote address, Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development, GoI, said that around 10 crore women organised into nearly 92 lakh SHGs have leveraged formal credit of about ₹14 lakh crore. The next phase must strengthen around 87 lakh enterprises and track the progress of Lakhpati Didis towards the target of six crore. He said “what gets measured gets done; what gets measured gets improved,” and called for LokOS to become an operational platform integrated with banking portals for a seamless digital credit journey. He urged that data be complete, consistent, current, correct and verifiable, and that the Mission move from monitoring dashboards to decision-support systems.
Shri Vipin Kumar, Additional Secretary, Department of Rural Development, GoI, outlined three strategic shifts for DAY-NRLM i.e. from inclusion to prosperity, from credit access to quality credit, and from supported to self-reliant institutions. He said LokOS can build a digital record of credibility for each woman based on her saving and repayment behaviour. He stressed that this data belongs to the women who generate it and must be used in their interest.
The Ministry has been closely working with the State Rural Livelihoods Missions and technical partners to systematically resolve operational and system-related issues, assign clear responsibilities and timelines, strengthen the training and handholding of field functionaries and community cadres, and facilitate cross-learning through the replication of State best practices. Progress in digitising SHG, VO and CLF profiles and recording their financial transactions on LokOS was reviewed during the workshop. Validation of member and institution data was stated to be the foundation for transactions, credit histories and programme analysis. The workshop will strengthen the monitoring framework by moving to household, institutional and enterprise outcomes, using LokOS as an evidence base, connecting administrative datasets across schemes, and investing in State capacity to generate and use evidence

articles.full_content:
Mumbai : 14 October 2026
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Western Regional Office, Mumbai, celebrated World Standards Day 2026 through ‘Manak Mahotsav’ at Bharat Ratnam Mega Common Facility Centre (CFC), SEEPZ MIDC, Andheri (East), Mumbai. The event focused on Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7): Affordable and Clean Energy, highlighting the vital role of Indian Standards in promoting energy efficiency, clean energy technologies, industrial sustainability, and access to safe and reliable energy solutions.
The programme brought together academicians, industry representatives, technical experts and BIS officials to deliberate on the contribution of standardisation to sustainable development and India's transition to cleaner energy systems.
Padma Vibhushan Prof. M. M. Sharma, former Director of the University Department of Chemical Technology (UDCT), now the Institute of Chemical Technology (ICT), Mumbai, was the Chief Guest. The programme commenced with the lighting of the ceremonial lamp, followed by the welcome address by Scientist-F and Head, Mumbai Branch Office, BIS, Shri Rajeev Ranjan Singh. Deputy Director General (West), BIS, Shri Subhadip Basu, delivered the inaugural address, highlighting the importance of standards in advancing quality, innovation and sustainable development. Scientist-E and Head, Western Regional Laboratory, BIS, Dr. Anil Kapri, conveyed the World Standards Day message.
The Guests of Honour, Director, Statcon Energiaa, Shri Pranjal Pande, and Chief CRM & Tubes, Tata Steel, Shri Shashi Bhushan, shared their perspectives on the importance of quality, standardisation and technological innovation in supporting sustainable industrial practices and the development of clean energy solutions. Chief Guest Prof. M. M. Sharma emphasised the importance of scientific advancement, technological innovation and quality-oriented approaches in addressing emerging industrial and sustainability challenges. The session underscored the need to leverage scientific knowledge and standardisation to support sustainable industrial growth and the development of energy-efficient and environmentally responsible technologies.
A felicitation ceremony was organised to recognise recipients of All India First Licences, well-performing Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs), laboratories and other stakeholders for their contributions to strengthening quality infrastructure and promoting BIS initiatives.

articles.title: MANAGE Observes National Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026, Highlights Women's Role in Viksit Krishi
articles.full_content:
The National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management (MANAGE), under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India, organised National Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 on the theme “Role of Women Farmers in Building a Developed Agriculture and a Developed India” at Krishi Chanakya Auditorium, MANAGE, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad.
Dr. Veenita Kumari Menon, Deputy Director General, MANAGE, along with other dignitaries, inaugurated the event.
The event celebrated the vital contributions of women farmers in Indian agriculture, recognising their role in driving agricultural development, strengthening rural livelihoods, and promoting entrepreneurship and innovation towards Viksit Krishi and Viksit Bharat 2047.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Veenita Kumari Menon, Deputy Director General, MANAGE, highlighted the Government of India’s commitment to addressing farmers’ needs through various schemes, programmes and missions, including the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN), Kisan Credit Card (KCC), Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana and Agriculture Infrastructure Fund. She encouraged farmers to access these schemes and avail themselves of the benefits, particularly those who may be unaware of them. Several other missions are also being implemented, including initiatives relating to oil palm and edible oils, which also benefit women farmers.
She highlighted the Namo Drone Didi initiative and the contributions of Krishi Sakhis to natural farming. She also noted that digital mobile applications can help farmers use technology in agricultural activities. As India moves towards Viksit Bharat 2047, women farmers were encouraged to focus on value addition, food processing and entrepreneurship to enhance their incomes. She stressed the importance of accessing state, national and export markets by ensuring product quality and obtaining the necessary certifications.
Women entrepreneurs from Telangana, Goa, Gujarat, Odisha and Nagaland shared their achievements in agriculture and allied sectors. Their initiatives included beekeeping and honey production, rice noodle manufacturing, food processing, catering, natural farming, agricultural training and millet-based food enterprises. Their experiences highlighted how women are creating livelihood opportunities and strengthening rural enterprises through their work across these sectors.
Mrs. Trishavanti Sanjana, a farmer entrepreneur from Telangana, shared her experience in beekeeping and honey production, highlighting how the enterprise can promote women’s skill development and entrepreneurship. She emphasised that maintaining product quality, gradually expanding the customer base and seeking guidance from experienced professionals were key to building a profitable business. She established her honey enterprise using her savings and also provides free training to women farmers and Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs).

ICAR-CIWA Celebrates Rashtriya Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026
articles.full_content:
The ICAR–Central Institute for Women in Agriculture (ICAR-CIWA), Bhubaneswar, commemorated Rashtriya Mahila Kisan Diwas today, aligning with the global observance of the International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026. The convention brought together over 250 participants—including women farmers, Self-Help Group (SHG) members, Women Farmer Producer Organizations (WFPOs), students, and agricultural scientists—to recognize and advance the role of women in agriculture.
Welcoming the delegates, Dr. Mridula Devi, Director of ICAR-CIWA, highlighted the institute’s commitment to developing gender-responsive technologies, building capacity, and creating sustainable livelihood models. She emphasized that targeted skill training, technology transfer, and institutional support are essential to enhancing farm productivity and expanding rural women's entrepreneurship.
Chief Guest Shri Sachin Ramchandra Jadhav, IAS, Commissioner-cum-Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Empowerment, Government of Odisha, stressed that closing the gender gap and ensuring equal opportunity are vital to realizing the sector's full potential. He commended ICAR-CIWA for formulating state-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for farm machinery, enabling women farmers to operate equipment safely and independently. Shri Jadhav also called for collaborative policy interventions between ICAR-CIWA and the state government to strengthen women’s land rights. Guest of Honour Prof. S. Pasupalak, Former Vice-Chancellor of OUAT, urged women farmers to leverage collective group action and highlighted the importance of impact assessments for women-friendly agricultural implements.
A major milestone of the celebration was the distribution of ICAR-CIWA’s pedal-operated coconut dehusker to 50 women SHGs to mitigate physical drudgery, prevent occupational hazards, and enhance household incomes. Participants also explored dynamic demonstrations of farm innovations, including agricultural drones, the Integrated Vertical Nutri Farming System (IVNFS), hydroponics, mushroom cultivation, disc ridgers, and maize dehusker-cum-shellers.
The event honored six progressive women farmers for their exceptional contributions to agricultural production and allied enterprises. The day concluded with an interactive scientist–farmer interface focused on climate-resilient farming practices, improved crop varieties, and modern farm management strategies.
